name: Bell-LaPadula access-control decisions and label lattice
theory_paragraphs: In a \term{multilevel security (MLS)} system every subject and object carries a \term{security label} $L = (SL, C)$: a \term{sensitivity level} $SL$ from a linear order (e.g. Unclassified $<$ Confidential $<$ Secret $<$ Top Secret, abbreviated $U < C < S < TS$) and a set of \term{compartments} $C$ enforcing need-to-know. Labels are compared by \term{dominance}: $L_1 = (SL_1, C_1) \sqsubseteq L_2 = (SL_2, C_2)$ iff $SL_1 \leq SL_2$ \emph{and} $C_1 \subseteq C_2$. Dominance is only a \term{partial order}: two labels may be \term{incomparable} (neither dominates the other), typically because each has a compartment the other lacks. The labels form a lattice with bottom (lowest level, $\emptyset$) and top (highest level, all compartments).

\term{Bell--LaPadula (BLP)} is a \term{mandatory access control (MAC)} model: a central policy, not the owner, decides access, and its two rules prevent information from flowing to lower labels. \term{No read up} (\term{simple security property}, ss-property): subject $s$ may \emph{read} object $o$ iff $f_o(o) \sqsubseteq f_s(s)$, i.e. the object's label is dominated by the subject's (clearance) label. \term{No write down} (\term{star property}, $*$-property): $s$ may \emph{write} $o$ iff $f_c(s) \sqsubseteq f_o(o)$, i.e. the subject's (current) label is dominated by the object's. Writing \emph{up} is allowed --- a secret subject may deposit data in a top-secret file it cannot read (a \term{blind write}); writing \emph{down} is forbidden so secrets cannot be leaked into low-classified objects (e.g. by a Trojan horse running at the subject's level).

Access modes matter: \term{read} and \term{write} are checked by the two rules above; some models state that write implies read, in which case a write request must satisfy \emph{both} rules, while \term{append} (write-only) is governed by the $*$-property alone --- so append up is allowed even when read is denied. Some problems tabulate both a \term{maximum clearance} $f_s$ and a \term{current clearance} $f_c$ per subject; read requests are typically checked against the maximum, write requests against the current level (read the problem statement for its convention). Exceptions (declassification, sanitization) require \term{trusted subjects} outside the two rules --- mention this only if asked about the model's limits.
theory_cheatsheet: Label: $L = (SL, C)$; dominance $L_1 \sqsubseteq L_2$ iff $SL_1 \leq SL_2$ AND $C_1 \subseteq C_2$ --- \imp{both conditions must hold}.
\imp{No read up (ss-property):} read $o$ iff $f_o(o) \sqsubseteq f_s(s)$ (object dominated by subject).
\imp{No write down (*-property):} write $o$ iff $f_c(s) \sqsubseteq f_o(o)$ (subject dominated by object).
Write-up / blind write is legal; write-down is the leak BLP forbids.
\imp{Incomparable labels} (neither $L_1 \sqsubseteq L_2$ nor $L_2 \sqsubseteq L_1$) $\Rightarrow$ \imp{neither read nor write}.
Append = write-only: only the $*$-property applies; write-implies-read needs both rules. No compartments $\Rightarrow$ dominance is just the linear level order.
identify_givens: A BLP system stated as: an ordered set of sensitivity levels (e.g. $U < C < S < TS$), optionally a set of compartments, the label form $L = (SL, C)$ with dominance $L_1 \sqsubseteq L_2$ iff $SL_1 \leq SL_2$ and $C_1 \subseteq C_2$, and concrete subject clearances $f_s$/$f_c$ and object classifications $f_o$ (given as tables or bullet lists). Access modes read, write (may imply read), append (write-only).
identify_target: Formally define no-read-up (ss-property) and no-write-down (*-property); then decide grant/deny for each listed (subject, object, mode) request with justification naming the rule violated when denied; possibly draw the label partial order (Hasse diagram over levels $\times$ compartment powerset) or construct example labels achieving a specified allowed/denied read/write combination.
strategy_name: Dominate-and-decide: formalize the two rules, then check dominance for each request

algorithm.detail: State the label order: for $L_1 = (SL_1, C_1)$ and $L_2 = (SL_2, C_2)$, $L_1 \sqsubseteq L_2$ iff $SL_1 \leq SL_2$ (linear level order) and $C_1 \subseteq C_2$ (compartment subset). \imp{Both conjuncts must hold.} If the problem has no compartments, dominance is just $SL_1 \leq SL_2$.

Write out the concrete label of every subject and object from the tables, e.g. Farah: $(S, \{N, E\})$, Bulletin: $(U, \{\})$. If both maximum clearance $f_s$ and current clearance $f_c$ are given, note which one each rule uses.

For each request state grant or deny plus the exact reason: which dominance holds or fails, and in case of denial name the violated rule (no read up / ss-property, or no write down / $*$-property). \imp{Incomparable labels: neither read nor write.}

If asked to draw the partial order: nodes are all (level, compartment-set) pairs; edges go from $(SL, C)$ to the next higher level with the same $C$ and to $(SL, C \cup \{x\})$ for each compartment $x \notin C$; bottom is (lowest level, $\emptyset$), top is (highest level, all compartments). If asked to invent labels for a desired outcome, run dominance in reverse: pick levels ordered as required and compartments as subset/superset (allowed) or incomparable sets (denied).

variations.name: Compartments vs no compartments
variations.detail: The HT2018 instance explicitly drops compartments (dominance = linear level order, incomparability impossible); newer exams add compartments, where the trap is comparing only levels and forgetting $C_1 \subseteq C_2$: equal levels with incomparable compartment sets (e.g. $\{N,E\}$ vs $\{N,W\}$) mean neither read nor write. Always check both components.

variations.name: Mode trap: append and write-implies-read
variations.detail: Append (write-only) up is allowed via the $*$-property even though a read would be denied --- the trap is refusing append because read fails. But append still needs full dominance: a level high enough does not rescue a failing compartment set. Conversely, if the stated model lets write imply read, a write request must satisfy both rules.

variations.name: Max vs current clearance
variations.detail: When both $f_s$ (max) and $f_c$ (current) are tabulated (HT2018: Bob max secret, current confidential), using the wrong function flips verdicts --- Bob's write to a secret file is denied because $f_c(\text{Bob}) \not\sqsubseteq f_o(\text{file})$ even though $f_s$ would allow it. Read the problem's convention before deciding.

variations.name: Construction and lattice-drawing subtasks
variations.detail: Instead of deciding requests, the exam may ask to draw the Hasse diagram of the label lattice or invent labels for a target outcome (read allowed: subject $(TS, \{A\})$, object $(S, \{A\})$; write allowed: subject $(S, \{A\})$, object $(TS, \{A\})$). Run the dominance checks in reverse: choose levels ordered as the target requires and compartments as subsets/supersets.

original_problem: A freight-rail operator protects infrastructure data with Bell--LaPadula. Sensitivity levels are $U < R < C < S < TS$ (Unclassified, Restricted, Confidential, Secret, Top Secret) and compartments are $\{N, E, W, K\}$ (the four lines North, East, West, Kargo). Subject clearances: Dispatcher Farah: $(S, \{N, E\})$; Auditor Bjorck: $(C, \{N, W\})$; Technician Osei: $(R, \{N\})$. Object classifications: Dossier: $(C, \{N, E\})$; Blueprint: $(TS, \{N, E, K\})$; Archive: $(C, \{N, W\})$; Log: $(C, \{N\})$; Bulletin: $(U, \{\})$. (a) Formally define the BLP properties \emph{no read up} and \emph{no write down}. (b) For each of the following, decide with justification whether access is granted or denied: Farah reads or writes Dossier and Blueprint; Bjorck reads or writes Archive and Dossier; Osei reads or writes Log and Bulletin. (c) Taking \emph{append} to be write-only: may Bjorck append to Blueprint? May Osei append to Blueprint? Justify.

original_steps.work: Dominance: $L_1 = (SL_1, C_1) \sqsubseteq L_2 = (SL_2, C_2)$ iff $SL_1 \leq SL_2$ and $C_1 \subseteq C_2$, with levels $U < R < C < S < TS$ and $C_i \subseteq \{N, E, W, K\}$.

(a) No read up (ss-property): subject $s$ may read object $o$ iff $f_o(o) \sqsubseteq f_s(s)$. No write down ($*$-property): $s$ may write $o$ iff $f_c(s) \sqsubseteq f_o(o)$. Append is write-only, so it requires only the $*$-property.

Instantiate: Farah $= (S, \{N,E\})$; Bjorck $= (C, \{N,W\})$; Osei $= (R, \{N\})$; Dossier $= (C, \{N,E\})$; Blueprint $= (TS, \{N,E,K\})$; Archive $= (C, \{N,W\})$; Log $= (C, \{N\})$; Bulletin $= (U, \{\})$.

Farah vs Dossier: read needs $L_{\text{Dos}} \sqsubseteq L_{\text{Farah}}$: $C \leq S$ and $\{N,E\} \subseteq \{N,E\}$ --- granted. Write needs $L_{\text{Farah}} \sqsubseteq L_{\text{Dos}}$: $S \not\leq C$ --- denied (no write down). Read-only. Farah vs Blueprint: read needs $TS \leq S$ --- false, denied (no read up). Write needs $S \leq TS$ and $\{N,E\} \subseteq \{N,E,K\}$ --- granted (blind write-up). Write-only.

Bjorck vs Archive: labels equal, $(C, \{N,W\}) \sqsubseteq (C, \{N,W\})$ in both directions ($C \leq C$, $\{N,W\} \subseteq \{N,W\}$) --- both read and write granted. Bjorck vs Dossier: read needs $\{N,E\} \subseteq \{N,W\}$ --- false ($E$ missing); write needs $\{N,W\} \subseteq \{N,E\}$ --- false ($W$ missing); levels equal but compartment sets incomparable --- neither read nor write. Osei vs Log: read needs $C \leq R$ --- false, denied (no read up); write needs $R \leq C$ and $\{N\} \subseteq \{N\}$ --- granted (write-up). Write-only. Osei vs Bulletin: read needs $U \leq R$ and $\{\} \subseteq \{N\}$ --- granted; write needs $R \leq U$ --- false, denied (no write down). Read-only.

(c) Append needs only the $*$-property. Bjorck append Blueprint: $(C, \{N,W\}) \sqsubseteq (TS, \{N,E,K\})$ requires $\{N,W\} \subseteq \{N,E,K\}$, which fails since $W \notin \{N,E,K\}$ --- denied, even though $C \leq TS$. Osei append Blueprint: $(R, \{N\}) \sqsubseteq (TS, \{N,E,K\})$ since $R \leq TS$ and $\{N\} \subseteq \{N,E,K\}$ --- granted (a blind write; Osei still may not read Blueprint). Final verdicts: Farah: Dossier read-only, Blueprint write-only; Bjorck: Archive read and write, Dossier neither; Osei: Log write-only, Bulletin read-only; appends: Bjorck denied, Osei granted.
